title: Welcome to DocNest
description: A quick orientation to DocNest — how to browse learning paths, search, and get the most out of each tutorial.

title: Python Fundamentals for Building with LLMs
description: Type hints, dictionaries, TypedDict, decorators, and async — the core Python concepts behind LangChain and LangGraph code.

title: Python Data Essentials
description: NumPy for fast math, pandas for labeled tables, and matplotlib for seeing your data — the data toolkit every ML project starts from.

title: Machine Learning Fundamentals
description: Features and labels, train/test splits, overfitting, and the split-fit-predict-score loop — with a working scikit-learn example.

title: Neural Networks from Scratch
description: Weights, activations, forward pass, and gradient descent — build a network by hand in NumPy, then see the same loop in PyTorch.

title: Transformers Explained
description: Attention, Query/Key/Value, multi-head heads, and why this architecture replaced RNNs — the foundation of every modern LLM.

title: How LLMs Actually Work
description: Tokens, next-token prediction, pretraining, and sampling — why models sound smart, why they hallucinate, and what it all means in practice.

title: Prompt Engineering Basics
description: How models read prompts, system vs. user messages, and the few techniques — few-shot, chain-of-thought, delimiters — that carry most real-world value.

title: Function Calling with LLM APIs
description: The raw mechanism under every agent: how a model requests a structured call to your code, and the send-execute-feed-back loop that powers it.

title: Building Your First LangChain Agent
description: A deep, beginner-friendly walkthrough of tools, agents, and the reasoning loop in LangChain, from first principles to a working JavaScript client.

title: Building Stateful Workflows with LangGraph
description: Learn how nodes, edges, and shared state let you build branching, looping workflows that go beyond a simple agent loop.

title: Building RAG Pipelines with Embeddings
description: Chunk, embed, store, retrieve — a complete minimal RAG pipeline that lets an LLM answer from your documents instead of hallucinating.

title: Agent Evaluation Fundamentals
description: What agent evaluation is, why it differs from software testing, the components worth measuring, and judging final answers vs. the path an agent took.

title: Building Evaluation Datasets for AI Agents
description: How to build the eval set itself — case structure, golden data, positive/negative/edge cases, representative tasks, and versioning the dataset like code.

title: Agent Evaluation Metrics
description: Task success rate, precision/recall, relevance, groundedness, tool-call accuracy, latency and cost — and how to choose which metrics matter for your agent.

title: Evaluating Agent Tool Calls
description: Correct tool selection, argument matching, call order, error recovery, and the hidden trap of unnecessary calls — with concrete good and bad examples.

title: Evaluating Agent Trajectories
description: How to judge the plan/act/observe loop itself: intermediate steps, efficiency, failure patterns, and how trajectory evaluation differs from final-answer evaluation.

title: LLM-as-a-Judge for Agent Evaluation
description: Designing judge prompts and rubrics, structured JSON scoring, and the biases that make LLM judges unreliable — with calibration and deterministic-check combinations.

title: Agent Evaluation and Regression Testing
description: Re-running a frozen eval suite after every change to catch regressions, comparing baselines without chasing noise, and wiring agent evals into CI/CD.

title: Agent Evaluation Techniques
description: From golden datasets to LLM-as-judge — how to systematically measure whether an agent actually works, and catch regressions.

title: Evaluating Agents in Production
description: Offline vs online evaluation, monitoring live quality, user feedback, sampling conversations, cost and latency, and privacy rules for evaluating on real user data.

title: Serving LLM Applications in Production
description: Latency budgets, streaming, rate limits, caching, retries, and logging — what changes when real users start hitting your LLM app.
